# 0005 — Conformance against R, Lean for transformation soundness

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-06-11

## Decision

Correctness gets three layers, with three different ground truths. None of
them is a substring assertion over emitted C.

1. **Accepted subset as a formal grammar.** The fragment of R we claim to
   compile is written as an explicit EBNF derived from R's own `gram.y`
   (the yacc grammar
   [`src/main/gram.y`](https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/blob/master/src/main/gram.y)).
   Every production has a disposition —
   `core` (compiled), `boundary` (lowered to `r_eval`), or `rejected`. This
   grammar *is* the spec boundary: the frontend must accept exactly the `core`
   + `boundary` surface and reject the rest, and the conformance generator
   draws only from it. See [`r-subset-grammar.md`](../r-subset-grammar.md).

2. **R itself is the conformance oracle (the Porffor discipline).** Every
   program in the subset is run two ways — compiled by `tccq` and evaluated by
   the R interpreter — and the results are diffed. This mirrors R's own
   `tests/*.Rout.save` golden-output regression method. We track a single
   **conformance number** (cases passing / cases total) and CI fails on any
   regression of it. Programs come from two sources: *generated* (the grammar
   driver, exhaustive over the subset's shapes) and *harvested* (in-subset
   fragments lifted from `r-svn/tests/`, e.g. `arith.R`, `any-all.R`,
   `primitives.R`).

3. **Lean 4 proves what the oracle cannot reach.** A differential oracle shows
   that *the cases we ran* matched R; it cannot show a *pass* preserves meaning
   for all inputs. So the LIR core ([0002](0002-lowered-ir-seam.md)) gets a
   denotational semantics in Lean, and each middle-end rewrite
   (index-normalize, kernelize, fusion, and the LIR→C-model lowering) is proved
   meaning-preserving over that core. Lean formalizes **our IR and our
   transformations**, and the elementwise/affine fragment of R semantics they
   depend on — not all of R.

## Why — the Porffor lesson

Porffor (an AOT JS/TS→Wasm/native compiler) does **not** use a theorem prover
to justify itself. It runs **test262**, ECMAScript's official executable
conformance suite, against the compiler and reports a tracked pass percentage
that CI guards. The "proof" is empirical conformance to the language's own spec
suite, never regressing.

R's equivalent of test262 already exists: the `make check` regression corpus in
`r-svn/tests/` with `.Rout.save` golden outputs. R is also runnable in-process
as a live oracle (`Rscript` 4.6.0 is present). So we can take Porffor's exact
discipline — spec suite as ground truth, tracked number, no-regression gate —
without inventing an oracle.

## Why we cannot just copy r-svn

Porffor targets *all* of JS, so test262 applies wholesale. We compile a
**subset** — `declare(type(...))`-annotated numeric kernels — so the vast
majority of `r-svn/tests/` (S4, datetime, IO, plotting, regex, package
machinery) is out of scope by construction. Copying it blindly would produce a
suite that is 90% skips and tests nothing about our compiler.

The transplantable parts are the *methodology* (golden diffing against R) and
the *idioms* — arithmetic, reductions, indexing, control flow — which we
**harvest** into the subset rather than import wholesale. The grammar (layer 1)
is what makes "in subset" a decidable question instead of a vibe.

## Why Lean, and its honest scope

The oracle suite is necessary but not sufficient: it validates sampled
behaviour, not transformation soundness. Constant-folding a loop, fusing a
producer into a fold, or normalizing an index chain are claims about *all*
inputs; a generator can only sample. These are exactly the claims a proof
assistant settles.

This document is itself checked: the proof below is compiled by Lean (via the
[`leanknit`](https://github.com/sounkou-bioinfo/leanknit) engine) at render
time. The `#print axioms` line is the trust base — if a `sorry` ever crept into
`TccqLir.fold_preserves`, this render would fail.

```{lean, axioms="TccqLir.fold_preserves"}
import TccqLir.Core
```

`[propext]` only: propositional extensionality, a standard logical axiom — no
`sorry`, not even classical choice. `fold_preserves` states that constant
folding preserves the denotation of the LIR value core for every environment.

What Lean does **not** do here: formalize the whole R language. No complete
formal semantics of R exists (the nearest prior art is the *core R* operational
semantics of Morandat et al., ECOOP 2012 — a subset, not the language).
Attempting full R in Lean would be a multi-year research project orthogonal to
shipping a transpiler, and pretending otherwise would be slop. Lean's remit is
bounded: the LIR core, its passes, and the slice of R semantics those passes
assume.

## What this rejects

- **Formalizing all of R in a prover.** Rejected as out of scope; Lean covers
  the LIR core and our passes only.
- **Copying `r-svn/tests/` wholesale.** Rejected; harvest in-subset fragments
  against the formal grammar instead.
- **Conformance without an oracle** (golden strings, source-substring checks as
  the *primary* signal). Rejected; R is the ground truth — prefer semantic and
  runtime tests over source-substring assertions.
- **A conformance number that can silently drop.** Rejected; CI gates on it.

## Consequences

- New artifacts: `docs/r-subset-grammar.md` (the formal EBNF + dispositions,
  layer 1), a conformance harness driving R-as-oracle with a tracked number
  (layer 2), and a Lean project under `proofs/` (layer 3, Lean 4.30.0 via elan,
  std only — no mathlib initially, to keep build time bounded).
- The existing generated differential tests
  (`test_tccq_generated_validation.R`) are the seed of layer 2 and get folded
  into the grammar-driven generator rather than living as an ad hoc set.
- Lean proofs are advisory until the LIR core stabilizes ([0002](0002-lowered-ir-seam.md)); they are written against the LIR node forms in
  `R/tccq_lir.R` and updated as that surface grows, pass by pass.
- Documents that state proofs are generated from `.Rmd` with the `leanknit`
  engine so the claim and the check cannot drift (`tools/render_docs.R`).
